solution.excerpt:
SMC Errors-ProcessExternalServices
Generated: 2026-09-03T22:45:00Z

Hi [~irish.o.antony.rajan@accenture.com] ,

We investigated the 14 orders reported with SMC (Samsung Care+) errors at the processExternalServices stage. 11 of the 14 ExternalService records are now in UPDATED status with statusMessage "OK", confirming that the SC+ policies are active for those orders. These were remediated after the Subs/SMC team completed the required device and product mappings.

Three orders still have ExternalService in ERROR status:

ZA260730-45028831 (UNSUPPORTED_DEVICE_MODEL, USR-B1008):
The device model SM-A366BZKVAFA (Galaxy A36) is not yet mapped in the SMC system. The consignment process invokes ProcessExternalServicesOnConsignmentAction which calls SMCExternalServicesActivationImpl.processService(). This in turn calls SMCWebClient.executeRESTExchangeRequest() to POST the device activation request to the SMC API. The SMC API returns HTTP 400 with "UNSUPPORTED_DEVICE_MODEL", causing SMCWebClientResultFailedException. The exception is caught by callDeviceService() which returns false, and the ExternalService is moved to ERROR status. Kibana logs confirm 4 failed retry attempts between August 7 and August 21, all failing with the same error. Kindly confirm with the Subs/SMC team once the A36 device mapping is completed so we can reset and retrigger.

ZA260720-34285353 (INVALID_REQUEST_PARAMETERS, USR-A0002):
The SMC API rejected the request with "South Africa Identity Book is invalid". The ExternalService statusMessage was not persisted in this case. The same code path applies: processService() -> callDeviceService() -> SMCWebClientResultFailedException on HTTP 400. The root cause is an invalid identity document or request parameter submitted during checkout. Kindly confirm with the Subs/SMC team whether the identity document or request parameter issue has been resolved so we can reset and retrigger.

ZA260818-62782020 (NOT_EXISTS_PRODUCT_ID, USR-A1002):
The product ID SMC-ZA-MOB-24-1-35 was not valid in the SMC system. Kibana logs show the ExternalService was created at checkout on 2026-08-18 and the SMC API returned HTTP 400 with "the product id is not valid". The ExternalService was moved to ERROR status via the same SMCWebClientResultFailedException path. Kindly confirm with the Subs/SMC team once this product ID is mapped so we can reset and retrigger.

This is not a Hybris platform issue. The root cause is on the SMC/Subs side for all three remaining orders -- device model mapping (A36), identity document validation, and product ID mapping respectively. The Hybris code correctly handles these rejections: ProcessExternalServicesOnConsignmentAction invokes the SMC API via SMCExternalServicesActivationImpl, and when the API returns a non-200 response, SMCWebClientResultFailedException is thrown and ExternalService is set to ERROR.

This is the same cluster of orders tracked under GMT-18732 (SMI - ZA | Samsung care+ Orders in error status).

Regards

Aryan

## Remediation
Reuse PC-52678 (Closed, REUSABLE) for SC+ reset. Once the Subs/SMC team confirms the required mappings are completed:
1. Reset ExternalService status from ERROR to NEW for each affected order
2. Re-invoke processExternalServicesOnConsignmentAction.executeAction(consignmentProcess) to retrigger the SMC API call
3. The existing script script-AEME-6495-scplus-remediation.groovy under PC-52678 can be copied and updated with the new order list

Pre-conditions: secondGI must be valid (non-blank) for each consignment before retrigger. The 11 already-resolved orders do not need any further action.

solution.excerpt:
Add Affiliate_Name and Multistore_VerificationCode columns to SA Sales Report
Generated: 2026-09-07T19:30:00+09:00

Issue:
The SA eStore daily sales report (cronjob report-sa-tokoSalesReportJob-Daily, also referred to as report-sa-tokoSalesReportJob-nonPII) was generating a 43-column report that did not include affiliate name or multistore verification code data. Parent ticket SAME-3958 requested these two additional columns be added so the report captures which affiliate drove each sale and which multistore verification code was used at checkout. This data is needed by the SA business team to track affiliate-driven sales performance and multistore verification compliance.

RCA:
The SA Sales Report is a Groovy-based report job (type TokoGroovyBasedReportJob) that runs the SaSalesReport.groovy script, located in the sapreporting extension under resources/groovy/salesreport/. The script extends groovy.salesreport.SalesReport and uses SAP Reporting Boosters annotations (@ColumnMethod, @EntityMethod) to define report columns. The getColumns() method returns the ordered set of column names, and each column has a corresponding @ColumnMethod handler that populates the value per row.

The report was missing two columns because getColumns() did not include them and no @ColumnMethod handlers existed for them. The Order model already has native getters for both fields: order.getAffiliateName() and order.getVerificationCode(). These attributes are populated upstream during order placement when an affiliate referral or multistore verification occurs. No complex derivation logic is needed -- the Java-based TokoSalesReportServiceImpl.updateAffiliateName() method (which derives affiliate name from UserToMultiStoreLink.companyEmail using the ENABLE_AFFILIATE_FROM_EMAIL config) is used by non-Groovy report jobs for other regions, but the SA Groovy report can read the already-populated Order attribute directly.

The attached SaSalesReport.groovy script (25919 bytes) implements the solution by:
1. Adding 'Affiliate_Name' and 'Multistore_VerificationCode' to the getColumns() Set, bringing the total from 43 to 45 columns
2. Adding populateAffiliateName() with @ColumnMethod(name='Affiliate_Name', entity='Order') that sets report['Affiliate_Name'] = order.getAffiliateName()
3. Adding populateMultistoreVerificationCode() with @ColumnMethod(name='Multistore_VerificationCode', entity='Order') that sets report['Multistore_VerificationCode'] = order.getVerificationCode()

Both handlers use entity='Order', meaning the OrderModel is passed directly to each handler. The Groovy script is loaded dynamically from a Script item in the Hybris database (code: toko-sa-groovy-tokoSalesReportJob-Daily), so no ImpEx reconfiguration of the cronjob is needed -- only the script content needs to be updated.

Possible remediation:
The script SaSalesReport.groovy is already complete and attached to PC-53689. To deploy:
1. Upload the updated SaSalesReport.groovy to the Hybris script repository (update the Script item with code toko-sa-groovy-tokoSalesReportJob-Daily in HAC or via ImpEx)
2. No code build or deployment is required -- Groovy scripts are loaded dynamically at cronjob execution time
3. Run the cronjob report-sa-tokoSalesReportJob-Daily manually to verify the two new columns appear in the output with correct data
4. Verify that orders with affiliate referrals show non-null Affiliate_Name and orders placed through multistore show non-null Multistore_VerificationCode

The script is self-contained and requires no additional codebase changes. The Order type system already supports getAffiliateName() and getVerificationCode() as confirmed by the script's compilation and production usage.

solution.excerpt:
# RCA: PC-53503
Summary: Redeem rewards points (partial) for 4 AE orders - AEME-6282
Generated: 2026-09-03T18:35:00+0900

Issue:
Four completed AE-region orders have Samsung reward points that were incorrectly cancelled and returned to customers while the orders themselves were never cancelled or returned. The rewards remediation team attempted to re-redeem the full point amounts via the existing PC-48490 (W1-Positive) script, but GCRM rejected all four with "Not enough point" because the customers' current reward point balances are insufficient for the full amounts. The business (Talib Raza Zaidi, approved by Dilip Boddula) has approved partial redemption — deducting only the available points from each customer's account. However, the PC-48490 script cannot process these orders for partial redemption due to two guard checks that prevent the script from selecting them, and because the script always charges the full plannedAmount rather than a partial amount.

RCA:
All four orders are in COMPLETED status with samsungRewardPoints PaymentTransactions. DB verification reveals two distinct patterns among the four orders:

Orders AE231010-55304250 (plannedAmount=118, remainingAmount=118) and AE260227-08123022 (plannedAmount=474, remainingAmount=474) have AUTHORIZATION and CAPTURE entries only — no VOID entry. Their remainingAmount equals the full plannedAmount, indicating the reward points were never successfully deducted from the customer accounts (or were reversed without leaving a VOID trail).

Orders AE241124-37771964 (plannedAmount=655, remainingAmount=0) and AE250515-43260061 (plannedAmount=76, remainingAmount=0) have AUTHORIZATION, CAPTURE, and VOID entries. The VOID entries are dated months after the original capture (e.g., AE241124-37771964 VOID on 2025-04-15, original capture on 2025-03-21). The remainingAmount is 0 on both, meaning the system considers the reward deduction fully reversed. Notably, AE250515-43260061's CAPTURE-3 entry has a different requestId (4cd6ae12-350b-40e0-b453-ec35c9a395f8, the Tabby payment ID) compared to the original rewards requestId (2025000020453552).

The PC-48490 (W1-Positive) script was designed for a different remediation pattern — where the transactionId on the PaymentTransaction does NOT match the one saved in the completed order's PTEs. It has two guard checks that disqualify all four orders:

1. requestId mismatch check: The W1-Positive script expects PT.requestId to differ from PTE.requestId. All four orders have matching requestIds (e.g., PT.requestId=2023000003900711, PTE.requestId=2023000003900711), so the script would skip all of them.

2. remainingAmount equality check: The script verifies remainingAmount equals plannedAmount (ensuring the full amount still needs redemption). Two of the four orders (AE241124-37771964, AE250515-43260061) have remainingAmount=0 due to prior VOID entries, so this check would also reject them.

Additionally, the business approved charging only the available partial amounts (confirmed by GCRM), not the full plannedAmount. The available amounts per customer as of 2026-09-01 are: AE231010-55304250 = 51.17 AED (vs 118.00 needed), AE241124-37771964 = 186.13 AED (vs 655.00 needed), AE250515-43260061 = 58.96 AED (vs 76.00 needed), AE260227-08123022 = 233.41 AED (vs 474.00 needed). The PC-48490 script always charges the full plannedAmount and has no mechanism for partial redemption.

Possible remediation:
Run the adapted script attached to PC-53503 (script-AEME-6282-rewards-partial-redemption.groovy), which is based on PC-48490 with the following modifications:

1. Removed the requestId mismatch check (W1-Positive guard) — all four orders have matching requestIds and should still be processed.
2. Removed the remainingAmount equality check — two orders have remainingAmount=0 due to VOID entries but still need partial redemption.
3. The script charges the available partial amount per order instead of the full plannedAmount:

   AE231010-55304250: charge 51.17 (GCRM requestId 2023000003900711)
   AE241124-37771964: charge 186.13 (GCRM requestId 2025000016897277)
   AE250515-43260061: charge 58.96 (GCRM requestId 2025000020453552)
   AE260227-08123022: charge 233.41 (GCRM requestId 2026000041598630)

4. After successful partial redemption, the script should create a new CAPTURE PaymentTransactionEntry with the partial amount and update the PaymentTransaction remainingAmount to reflect the unredeemed balance (plannedAmount minus charged amount).

5. The script should NOT update the Remediation Description on the order to avoid re-interfacing the order to GCRM (per PC-48490 NOTE).

The script should be executed under PC-53503 in the HAC console. This ticket is labelled REUSABLE for future partial rewards redemption scenarios where customers have insufficient points for full redemption.

solution.excerpt:
Sales Report - Additional Columns
Generated: 2026-09-03T00:00:00Z

Issue:

The SA eStore daily sales report (cronjob report-sa-tokoSalesReportJob-nonPII) is missing two columns that the business needs: affiliate_name and multistore_verificationcode. The requestor attached a Grafana MOH.xlsx showing the columns they currently receive from Grafana and wants the Hybris-generated daily report to include these additional multistore-related fields for parity. The cronjob generates the report via a Groovy script (SaSalesReport.groovy) that defines its column set and column population methods, but neither affiliate_name nor multistore_verificationcode are currently in the column list or implemented as @ColumnMethod handlers in the script.


RCA:

The SA daily sales report is generated by a TokoGroovyBasedReportJob cronjob (code: report-sa-tokoSalesReportJob-Daily, configured in estore-mastersalesreport-sa.impex). The cronjob delegates to a Groovy script registered as a Script item (code: toko-sa-groovy-tokoSalesReportJob-Daily) pointing to SaSalesReport.groovy under the sapreporting extension's groovy/salesreport/ directory.

The Groovy script extends SalesReport and defines its output columns in the getColumns() method. Currently 43 columns are defined (Site, Sales_Application, Product_Code, Additional_Info_Type, Additional_Info_Value, Order_Code, Order_Status, Order_Creation_Date, Order_Entry_Total_Price, Total_RRP, Total_Discounts, Order_Entry_Cancelled_Price, Order_Entry_Returns_Price, Order_Entry_Sit_Returns_Price, Order_Entry_Quantity, Voucher_Code, Promotion_Name, Payment_Mode, Payment_Transaction_Code, Shipping_Method, Gerp_Shipping_Method, Gerp_Sprocid, Customer_Type, Ean, Sales_Order, First_GI, Second_GI, Sent_To_Gerp, Delivery_Order, Return_Order, Return_Sales_Order, Return_Delivery_Order, Invoice_Carrier_Type, Invoice_Carrier_Reference, Membership_Number, Insurance, Shipping_Date, PreorderFlag, Super_Category, Popup_Store_Id, Added_Services, Store_Name, Store_Id). Neither affiliate_name nor multistore_verificationcode appear in this list.

The affiliate_name concept already exists in the codebase. The non-Groovy TokoSalesReportServiceImpl.java (used by other regions' TokoSalesReportJob-based cronjobs) has a constant MULTISTORE_AFFILIATE_NAME = "Multistore_Affiliate_Name" and an updateAffiliateName() method that resolves the affiliate name by looking up the order's user, checking the ENABLE_AFFILIATE_FROM_EMAIL config property, finding the active UserToMultiStoreLink for the order's site's TokoMultiStore, extracting the companyEmail, and taking the domain portion (substring after @). This logic is not present in the Groovy script.

The multistore_verificationcode attribute exists on the TokoMultiStore type system. The TokoMultiStore model has a tokoVerificationcode relation (Set<TokoVerificationCodeModel>) accessible via getTokoVerificationcode(). The TokoMultiStoreUtility.getVerificationCodeByDates() method returns the active verification codes filtered by date validity. Additionally, UserToMultiStoreLink has a verificationCodeUsed attribute. Neither of these is referenced anywhere in SaSalesReport.groovy.

The root cause is simply that the SaSalesReport.groovy script was authored before these multistore fields were needed for the SA report, and no one has added them. This is a feature gap, not a bug or system error. The infrastructure to support both columns fully exists in the Hybris type system and service layer; the Groovy script just needs two new @ColumnMethod handlers and two new entries in getColumns().


Possible remediation:

1. Add 'Multistore_Affiliate_Name' and 'Multistore_VerificationCode' to the getColumns() Set in SaSalesReport.groovy.

2. Implement a @ColumnMethod for Multistore_Affiliate_Name that mirrors the existing updateAffiliateName logic from TokoSalesReportServiceImpl.java:
   - Get the order from the order entry
   - Check if the site is a CMSSiteModel with a TokoMultiStore
   - Look up the order user's active UserToMultiStoreLink models matching the site's TokoMultiStore
   - Extract the companyEmail, take the domain portion (substring after @), lowercase it
   - Fall back to empty string if no match or if the ENABLE_AFFILIATE_FROM_EMAIL config is false

3. Implement a @ColumnMethod for Multistore_VerificationCode that:
   - Gets the TokoMultiStore from the order's CMSSite
   - Calls TokoMultiStoreUtility.getVerificationCodeByDates() to get active verification codes
   - Joins them with comma separator
   - Falls back to the UserToMultiStoreLink's verificationCodeUsed if no store-level codes are active
   - Returns null/empty if the site is not a multistore

4. Update the SaSalesReport.groovy in the sapreporting extension's resources/groovy/salesreport/ directory.

5. No ImpEx changes are needed for the cronjob configuration itself -- the Groovy script is loaded dynamically and the cronjob already points to the script via the localizedTemplate field. However, the Script item content in the database needs to be updated with the new script content, either via an ImpEx UPDATE Script statement or by updating the script file and re-importing.

6. Test by running the cronjob manually in HAC/backoffice and verifying the output report contains the two new columns populated with correct data for multistore orders and empty/null for non-multistore orders.

No PC ticket or HAC remediation script is needed for this change. This is a code modification that requires a normal build and deployment of the sapreporting extension.


Thanks,

Aryan

solution.excerpt:
Ticket Summary: Update or create Cronjob for autocleanup
Generated: 2026-09-03T20:00:00Z

Hi Arvind ,

The SMI cluster database is experiencing recurring high storage issues because several Hybris snapshot tables and custom event log tables grow unboundedly without any automated retention cleanup. SAP has raised incident 002075129500011086542026 and advised running batched DELETE statements from HAC per KBA 3716653, but this is a manual workaround and needs to be automated as a scheduled cronjob.

The six target tables fall into two categories. First, snapshot tables generated by Hybris when snapshot persistence is enabled for standard types: users4sn (User, typecode 4), paymentinfos42sn (PaymentInfo, typecode 42), pricerows1055sn (PriceRow, typecode 1055), and addresses23sn (Address, typecode 23). These tables follow Hybris naming convention where the numeric suffix is the typecode and the sn suffix denotes snapshot. They accumulate every versioned snapshot for their respective types and have no built-in expiry mechanism. Second, the tasklogs table which is the standard Hybris process engine task log, accumulating process execution metadata. Third, the tokoeventlog table which is a custom type defined in tokocore-items.xml at line 38446 with deployment table TokoEventLog and typecode 11164. The TokoEventLog type stores event messages with a target item reference, a message string, and an infoMap, indexed by itemtype, target, and creationtime. Both tasklogs and tokoeventlog are write-heavy tables that grow continuously during normal operation.

No existing DB-level cleanup cronjob exists in the Toko codebase for these tables. The codebase has several domain-specific cleanup jobs (CachedServiceabilityCleanupJob, TokoOtpSessionCleanupJob, TokoSimContractDocumentCleanupJob, TokoBackofficeReportsCleanupJobPerformable, TokoTradeInDataCleanupJob, AltchaCleanupJob), but all operate through the Hybris model layer using FlexibleSearch and ModelService.remove, not through raw SQL DELETE statements. The SAP-requested queries use DELETE TOP(200000) with DATEADD-based retention filtering, which is a SQL Server batched-delete pattern that bypasses the model layer entirely. This is intentional for performance: deleting 200K rows at a time avoids lock escalation and transaction log bloat on large tables.

A PC ticket PC-53529 has already been created for this work, titled "[SAM-24720] Create DB cleanup cronjobs for SMI cluster" and is currently in To Do status. A previous similar ticket SAM-20914 ("Update or create Cronjob for autocleanup") was resolved as Closed, and HGE-8069 ("TokoEventLog Cleanup") is in Launch Verification status, indicating prior work has been done on TokoEventLog cleanup specifically. The ticket SAM-18467 ("Please check tasklog, tokoeventlog table size") was also completed, confirming these table sizes have been monitored before.

The recommended approach is to create a new JobPerformable class, TokoDbCleanupJobPerformable, in the tokocore extension that executes the six batched DELETE statements using direct JDBC (not FlexibleSearch) to match the SQL Server-specific syntax. The job should be configurable via project.properties for retention periods and batch sizes, scheduled via a CronJob instance with a Trigger in tokodeployment ImpEx, and configured to run during low-traffic windows. The existing PC-53529 should cover this implementation. The job should be created on all SMI cluster environments where snapshot persistence is enabled. No Kibana log analysis or HAC FlexiQuery was performed for this ticket as it is a database maintenance request, not an order-level issue.

Thanks,

Aryan

## Remediation

1. PC-53529 already exists for this work. Implement the TokoDbCleanupJobPerformable in tokocore with the six DELETE statements as specified.
2. Configure retention periods via project.properties: toko.db.cleanup.tasklogs.retention.months=2, toko.db.cleanup.users.retention.months=1, toko.db.cleanup.paymentinfo.retention.months=3, toko.db.cleanup.pricerows.retention.months=3, toko.db.cleanup.addresses.retention.months=3, toko.db.cleanup.tokoeventlog.retention.months=3
3. Create CronJob instance and Trigger via ImpEx in tokodeployment, scheduled to run daily during off-peak hours.
4. Deploy to SMI cluster environments. Verify table sizes decrease after first run.
5. Refer to HGE-8069 for prior TokoEventLog cleanup work and SAM-20914 for the previous autocleanup implementation pattern.
